sources.title: Beike interview note containing the binary-tree longest-distance coding question
Structured repository question for binary-tree two-point longest distance
Deterministic Java and independent graph-oracle validation for binary-tree diameter

claims.text: The raw interview note asks for the longest distance between two points in a binary tree but does not define whether distance is measured in edges or path nodes; the candidate preserves that ambiguity instead of presenting a platform convention as source fact.

For edge-count diameter, a postorder traversal can return each node's maximum downward depth in nodes; if left and right returned depths are L and R, L+R is exactly the number of edges on the longest path whose lowest common ancestor is that node.

Taking the maximum L+R over every node covers every endpoint pair because each simple path has a lowest common ancestor at which its two downward portions are represented; paths contained entirely in a subtree are therefore not missed.

The exact Java implementation passes fixed empty/single/chain/balanced/subtree-diameter cases and 3000 deterministic random trees against an all-pairs BFS graph oracle; each tree node is visited once by the candidate algorithm, giving O(n) time and O(h) recursive-stack space.

checks: 3000 deterministic random trees versus structurally different all-pairs BFS oracle

findings: The candidate does not silently choose a source-unstated distance convention: it answers in edge count while explicitly mapping the node-count convention.
The recursive return value and the global diameter state are cleanly separated, preventing the common state-definition error.
The lowest-common-ancestor argument explains why updating L+R at every node covers paths that do not pass through the tree root.
The exact code is exercised against a structurally different all-pairs BFS oracle on 3000 deterministic random trees, in addition to fixed edge cases.
Complexity and recursion-depth boundaries are stated with their preconditions rather than as unconditional claims.
No production experience or hidden input contract is fabricated; required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
